questions.explanation: Reversing the passive voice, "by him" becomes the subject "He," followed by the active modal "must have stolen," and the object "it."

questions.question: You should have done it.[]
options: You should have done it.
It should have been done by you.
It should have done by you.
It would have been done by you.
questions.explanation: You should have done it" becomes "It should have been done by you." Option B is the only one that uses the correct "have been done" passive construction.

questions.question: Obey your parents.[]
options: Your parents were obeyed.
Your parents must be obeyed.
Your parents are to be obeyed.
Your parents should be obeyed.
questions.explanation: While "Let your parents be obeyed" is a standard imperative conversion, "Your parents should be obeyed" is frequently used to express the sense of moral duty inherent in the verb "obey."

questions.question: Shut the door at once.[]
options: The door be shut at once.
Let the door be shut at once.
Let the door shut at once.
The door be shuted at once.
questions.explanation: "Shut the door" follows the "Let + Object + be + V_3" structure. Thus, it becomes "Let the door be shut at once."

questions.question: Open the window.[]
options: The window should be opened.
Let the window be opened.
Let the window be opened by you.
The window must be opened.
questions.explanation: "Open the window" becomes "Let the window be opened." Option C is also grammatically possible, but B is the most standard, concise form.

questions.question: Always speak the truth.[]
options: Let the truth be spoked always.
Let the truth be spoken always.
Let the truth had spoken always.
Let the truth was spoken always.
questions.explanation: Using the structure Let + Object + be + V_3, it becomes "Let the truth be spoken always." Note that the past participle of "speak" is "spoken."

questions.question: Let him be told to go' change the voice is -----[]
options: Go
Let you go
You go
Tell him to go
questions.explanation: The passive command "Let him be told to go" reverses to the active command "Tell him to go."

questions.question: What is the passive voice "Do away with it" ?[]
options: Let it be done away with.
Let it has been away with.
Let it is to be done away with.
Let it has to do away with.
questions.explanation: "Do away with" is a phrasal verb. When converted to passive, the phrasal verb remains intact: "Let it be done away with."

questions.question: Tell him to go.[]
options: Let him told to go.
Let him be told to go.
Let he be told to go.
Let him tell to be gone.
questions.explanation:
"Let" + "him" (object) + "be" + "told" (V_3 of 'tell') + "to go."
âThis results in: "Let him be told to go."

questions.question: Don't do it.[]
options: Let not it be done.
Let it be not done.
Let it be done not.
Let it not be done.
questions.explanation: Let" + "it" (object) + "be" + "not" + "done" (V_3 of 'do').

questions.question: Don't neglect the poor.[]
options: Let the poor be neglected.
Let not the poor be neglected.
Let not the poor neglected.
Poor don't be neglected.
questions.explanation: The object is "the poor." Following the structure: "Let" + "the poor" + "not be" + "neglected" (V_3 of neglect). Thus, "Let not the poor be neglected."

questions.question: Do not open the door.[]
options: Let not the door be opened.
Let not the door open.
Let not the door be open.
Let not the door opened.
questions.explanation: The object is "the door." Following the structure: "Let" + "not" + "the door" + "be" + "opened" (V_3 of open). Thus, "Let not the door be opened."

questions.question: Let her sing a song.[]
options: Let a song be sung by her.
Let a song be sang by her.
Let a song sing by her.
Let a song sung by her.
questions.explanation: "Let her sing a song" converts by moving "a song" to the position after "Let." The verb "sing" becomes the past participle "sung." Thus, "Let a song be sung by her."

questions.question: Let me do the work.[]
options: Let the work done me.
Let the work be done.
Let me be done the work.
Let the work be done by me.
questions.explanation: In "Let me do the work," "the work" is the object that moves to the position after "Let."

questions.question: Let me write a letter.[]
options: Let a letter be write by me.
Let a letter be written by me.
Let a letter to write by me.
Let a letter is written by me.
questions.explanation: The object "a letter" moves after "Let." The verb "write" becomes the past participle "written," and "me" becomes the agent "by me."

questions.question: Never catch the Jatka.[]
options: Let the Jatka never be caught.
Let not the Jatka ever be caught.
Never the Jatka be caught by you.
The Jatka is caught by you.
questions.explanation: To maintain the negative "never" meaning in a passive construction, we use "Let not... ever be caught." This clearly conveys the instruction that the action should not take place.

questions.question: You are requested not to smoke.[]
options: No smoking is requested.
Please do not smoke.
You need not smoke.
Smoke not is requested.
questions.explanation: To convert this to active voice, you remove the passive markers "You are requested" and use the imperative form: "Please do not smoke" or simply "Do not smoke

questions.question: Enter the house by this gate.[]
options: You are requested to enter the house by this gate.
You should enter the house by this gate.
Let the house be entered by this gate.
Let the house be entered by you by this gate.
questions.explanation: In this case, "Enter the house by this gate" is a directive. Option A uses the "You are requested to..." structure, which is a grammatically standard way to convert this imperative into passive voice

questions.question: You are requested to give me a cup of tea.[]
options: Give me a cup of tea.
Let me give a cup of tea.
Please give me a cup of tea.
None
questions.explanation: The active voice equivalent of "You are requested to help me" is simply the request: "Please help me."

questions.question: You are requested to go there.Change the voice.[]
options: Go there.
Go you there.
Go
Requested to go
questions.explanation: When you see "You are requested to...", it indicates an imperative sentence (a request). To convert this to the active voice, remove the passive markers ("You are requested") and use the verb in its base form.

questions.question: Bring me a pen.[]
options: Let a pen be brought by me.
Let a pen be brought me.
Let me be brought by a pen.
Let a pen be brought for me.
questions.explanation: Bring me a pen," the action is performed "for" the speaker. Therefore, the passive construction becomes "Let a pen be brought for me".

questions.question: Give me your watch.[]
options: Let your watch be given to me.
Let your watch be given for me.
Let your watch is given me.
Let your watch is given to me.
questions.explanation:
This is an imperative sentence with two objects: the indirect object ("me") and the direct object ("your watch").
âThe standard passive structure for this type of imperative is: Let + direct object + be + past participle + to/for + indirect object.

questions.question: Pluck me a flower.[]
options: Let a flower be plucked me.
Let a flower be plucked to me.
Let a flower be plucked for me.
Let a flower be plucked by me.
questions.explanation: In "Pluck me a flower," the action is performed "for" the speaker. Therefore, the passive construction becomes "Let a flower be plucked for me".

questions.question: Bring me the book.[]
options: Let the book be brought for me.
Let the book be brought by me.
The book is brought for me.
The book is brought by me.
questions.explanation: In this context, bringing a book is typically done "for" someone. Thus, the passive voice is formed as: "Let the book be brought for me".

questions.question: Spread a mat on it.[]
options: A mat should be spread on it.
A mat should have been spread on it by you.
A mat be spread on it.
Have a mat spread on it.
questions.explanation: This is a causative construction where you are requesting that something be done for you. The structure Have + object + past participle is used to indicate that you want the action performed. Therefore, "Have a mat spread on it" is the correct passive form in this context.

questions.question: Did Samira do the work ?[]
options: Was the work by Samira done ?
Was the work done by Samira ?
Is the work done by Samira ?
Was not the work done by Samira ?
questions.explanation: To convert a simple past interrogative sentence into passive voice, use the structure: Was/Were + object + past participle + by + subject?.

questions.question: Does he speak English well ?[]
options: Is English spoke well by him ?
Is English spoken well to him ?
Is English spoken well by him ?
Was English spoken well by him ?
questions.explanation:
The object is "English".
âThe verb "speak" in its past participle form is "spoken".
âTherefore, the correct passive voice would be: "Is English spoken well by him?".

questions.question: Do you want me ?[]
options: Am I wanted to you ?
Am I want by you ?
Am I wanted by you ?
Am I want to you ?
questions.explanation: To convert an interrogative sentence in the Simple Present tense, use the formula: Is/Am/Are + object + past participle + by + subject?.

questions.question: Did you not read the book ?[]
options: Was the book not read by you ?
Was not the book read by you ?
Did the book not read by you ?
Did not the book read by you ?

questions.question: Did he read books ?[]
options: Does books read by him ?
Books are read by him ?
Are books read by him ?
Is books read by him ?
questions.explanation: For a negative interrogative sentence in the Simple Past, the passive structure is: Was/Were + not + object + past participle + by + subject?.

questions.question: Did you eat the mango ?[]
options: The mango was eaten by you ?
Was the mango eaten by you ?
By you was the mango eaten ?
Was the mango by you eaten ?
questions.explanation: To convert a simple past interrogative sentence into the passive voice, the formula is: Was/Were + object + past participle + by + subject?.

questions.question: Is he eating fruit ?[]
options: Is fruit eaten by him ?
Is fruit being eaten by him ?
Is fruit eating by him ?
Is fruit be eating by him ?
questions.explanation: When converting "ing" forms to passive, you must use being + V3 (past participle).

questions.question: Who taught you French ?[]
options: By whom you were taught French ?
By whom French was taught you ?
French was taught you by whom ?
By whom were you taught French ?
questions.explanation:
The "Who" Rule: In passive questions, "Who" usually changes to "By whom."
âSubject-Verb Agreement: Because the object is "you," the helping verb must be "were" (not was).

questions.question: Who taught you English ?[]
options: By whom you were taught English ?
By whom English was taught to you ?
English was taught to you by whom ?
By whom were you taught English ?
questions.explanation:
The "Who" Rule: In passive voice, "Who" must change to "By whom" at the beginning of the sentence.
âThe Verb "Taught": This is Simple Past. The passive form requires was/were + V3 (taught).

questions.question: Who gave you this pen ?[]
options: By whom were you got this pen ?
By whom were you given this pen ?
By whom were you have been given this pen ?
By whom was you given this pen ?
questions.explanation:
Since the object is "you," you must use "were." Options that use "was" (like D) are grammatically incorrect with "you."
âPast Participle: The passive voice always uses the V3 form. The V3 of "give" is given

questions.question: Who will do the work ?[]
options: Who will done the work ?
Who will be done the work ?
By whom will the work be done ?
By whom the work will be done ?
questions.explanation: In passive voice, "Who" changes to "By whom". Since the original sentence is in the Future Indefinite tense (will do), the passive structure requires will + be + past participle (V3).

questions.question: Who has written Hamlet ?[]
options: Hamlet has written by whom ?
By whom is Hamlet written ?
Who has Hamlet been written by ?
By whom Hamlet is written ?
questions.explanation: This is in the Present Perfect tense (has written). The passive form needs has/have + been + V3.

questions.question: Who is calling me ? (Passive)[]
options: By whom am I called ?
By whom I am called ?
By whom I was called ?
By whom am I being called ?
questions.explanation: This is the Present Continuous tense (is calling). Passive voice for continuous tenses requires the word "being".

questions.question: Who killed the bird ?[]
options: Who was killed by the bird ?
Who was killed the bird ?
Whom was killed by the bird ?
By whom was the bird killed ?
questions.explanation: When an active sentence starts with "Who," the passive version usually begins with "By whom." * Since "killed" is in the simple past tense, we use the auxiliary verb "was" followed by the past participle of the verb.

questions.question: Whom do you want ?[]
options: Whom is wanted by you ?
Who is wanted by you ?
By whom are you wanted ?
By whom you are wanted ?
questions.explanation: When the active sentence starts with "Whom" (the object), the passive version starts with "Who" (the new subject).

questions.question: Whom does he love ?[]
options: Who is loved by him ?
Who was loved by him ?
Who had he loved ?
Who loves him ?
questions.explanation: the active "Whom" becomes the passive "Who."

questions.question: Whom did she accuse ?[]
options: Who was accused by her ?
Who had been accused by her ?
Who was being accused by her ?
Who has been accused by her ?
questions.explanation: The active voice is in Simple Past. To convert to passive, the object "whom" becomes the subject "who," followed by the auxiliary "was" and the past participle "accused."

questions.question: What do you want ?[]
options: What was wanting by you ?
What is wanted by you ?
What was wanted by you ?
What is wanting by you ?
questions.explanation: The active voice is in Simple Present. In the passive structure, the auxiliary verb "is" is used because "what" acts as a singular subject, followed by the past participle "wanted."

questions.question: What made the noise ?[]
options: By what was the noise made ?
By what the noise was made ?
What was made the noise ?
What was the noise made ?
questions.explanation: When "what" is the subject of an active sentence, the passive form begins with "By what." In interrogative passive sentences, the auxiliary verb (was) must precede the subject (the noise).

questions.question: Where did you see him ?[]
options: Where did he seen by you ?
Where was he see by you ?
Where was seen by you ?
Where was he seen by you ?
questions.explanation: In interrogative sentences starting with "Where," the word order is: Question Word + Auxiliary + Subject + Past Participle. Since the active sentence is in Simple Past ("did see"), we use "was" and the third form of the verb ("seen").

questions.question: How can you do this ? (Passive)[]
options: How this can be done by you ?
How could this be done by you ?
How can this be done by you ?
How this could be done by you ?
questions.explanation: When modal verbs like "can" are used, the passive voice structure is: Modal + Object + be + Past Participle. The modal "can" remains in the sentence; we do not change it to "could" (which would be the past tense).

questions.question: Why did your brother write such a letter ?[]
options: Why was such a letter written by your brother ?
Why such a letter was written by your brother ?
Why such a letter was written by your brother.
Why was such a letter been written by your brother ?
questions.explanation: The sentence is in Simple Past. The structure follows: Why + was + object (such a letter) + V3 (written) + by + agent (your brother).

questions.question: When did he finish the work ? (Passive)[]
options: When the work was finished by him ?
When did the work finished by him ?
When was the work to be finished by him ?
When was the work finished by him ?
questions.explanation: This follows the standard interrogative structure for Simple Past passive: Question word (When) + auxiliary (was) + object (the work) + past participle (finished) + agent (by him).

questions.question: I saw him playing football.[]
options: Football was played and seen by him.
He was seen playing football by me.
Football was being played and seen by him.
Football was seen played by me and him.
questions.explanation: In sentences with a primary verb and a participle phrase (like "playing football"), we convert the primary verb ("saw") into the passive voice ("was seen") while keeping the secondary action attached to the object.

questions.question: He was seen by me carrying a basket.[]
options: I see him carrying a basket.
I had seen him carrying a basket.
I saw him carrying a basket.
He saw me carrying a basket.
questions.explanation: To convert from passive to active, the agent ("by me") becomes the subject ("I"), and the passive verb "was seen" reverts to its active form ("saw"). The participial phrase ("carrying a basket") remains attached to the object ("him").

questions.question: You made him cook rice.[]
options: He was made to cook rice.
He was made cook rice.
He is made to cook rice.
He had made to cook rice.
questions.explanation: This involves a causative verb ("made"). When converting "made + [object] + [bare infinitive]" to passive voice, the "bare infinitive" (cook) must change into a "full infinitive" (to cook).

questions.question: He heard her sing.[]
options: She was heard to sing by him.
She was heard sing by him.
She was heard to sing.
She was heard to be sing.
questions.explanation: Similar to Q20, verbs of perception like "hear," "see," or "watch" are followed by a bare infinitive in the active voice ("sing"). When converted to passive, that bare infinitive must change to a full infinitive ("to sing").

questions.question: I saw him go.[]
options: He is seen to go by me.
He was seen to go by me.
He is being go by me.
He has seen to go by me.
questions.explanation: This is a classic case of a sensory verb ("saw") followed by a bare infinitive ("go"). In the passive voice, the verb "saw" becomes "was seen," and the bare infinitive "go" must be converted to a full infinitive ("to go").

questions.question: They made him tell them everything.[]
options: He was made by them to tell them everything.
He was made to tell them everything.
He was made by them to tell everything to them.
Everything was made to be told them by him.
questions.explanation: When using the causative verb "made" in the active voice, it takes a bare infinitive ("tell"). When shifting to passive, "made" becomes "was made," and the infinitive must change to the full form ("to tell"). Option B is the most concise and grammatically standard way to express this

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: He was let go.
He was let to go.
He was let going.
He was letting go.
questions.explanation: While other causative verbs (like "make") require the "to" infinitive in passive voice, the verb "let" is an exception. In the passive voice, it retains the bare infinitive (without "to").

questions.question: He helped me do it.[]
options: It was done by him to help me.
I was helped by him to do it.
It was helped me by him to do it.
I was helped by him do it.
questions.explanation: The verb "help" can be followed by a bare infinitive in the active voice ("helped me do"). However, when converted to the passive voice, it must be followed by the full infinitive ("to do").

questions.question: I found it easy to do.[]
options: It was found easy to do by me.
It was found easy to be done by me.
It was easy found to do by me.
None of these
questions.explanation: This is a transformation of a complex sentence structure. We move the object ("it") to the subject position of the passive sentence, followed by the passive verb ("was found"), the adjective/complement ("easy to do"), and finally the agent ("by me").

questions.question: They elected him chairman.[]
options: He was elected chairman (by them).
Chairman was elected by them.
Chairman was elected him by them.
By them was he elected chairman.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses a "factitive verb" (a verb that requires an object and a complement, like elect, name, call, appoint). In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence ("him") becomes the subject ("He"), and the complement ("chairman") remains to describe the subject.

questions.question: He is thought to be a teacher.[]
options: We thought him to be a teacher.
We think him to be a teacher.
We think him a teacher.
We thought him a teacher.
questions.explanation: This is a passive construction involving an impersonal report or opinion. Since the passive verb is "is thought" (present tense), the active counterpart must be "We think" (present tense) followed by the object and the infinitive phrase.

questions.question: He is thought to be a poet by them.[]
options: They thought him to be poet.
They think him to be a poet.
They think to him be a poet.
They think him be a poet.
questions.explanation: the passive "is thought" indicates a present tense active verb ("think"). The agent "by them" becomes the subject "They." The structure follows: Subject (They) + Verb (think) + Object (him) + Complement/Infinitive phrase (to be a poet).

questions.question: Iron feels hard.[]
options: Iron is hard by it is felt.
Iron is hard when it is felt.
Hard feels by Iron.
Iron was hard.
questions.explanation: When a linking verb describes a sensory quality, we keep the subject ("Iron") and the adjective ("hard"), then add the clause "when it is felt" to explain how that state is determined.

questions.question: The pill tastes bitter.[]
options: The pill is bitter when it is tasted.
The pill is bitter when it was tasted.
The pill is bitter when it tasted.
The pill is bitter when it tastes.
questions.explanation: the verb "tastes" refers to the quality of the subject. The passive construction requires us to state the quality ("is bitter") and add the passive condition ("when it is tasted"). Option B is incorrect because "was" changes the tense unnecessarily.

questions.question: Honey tastes sweet.[]
options: Honey is tasted sweet.
Honey is sweet when it is tasted.
It is sweet when honey tasted.
Honey is sweet to taste.
questions.explanation:
Subject: Honey
âState: is sweet
âCondition: when it is tasted

questions.question: Rice sells cheap.[]
options: Rice is cheap when it is sold.
Rice is cheap sold.
Rice is being sold cheap.
Rice is cheap when it is selling.
questions.explanation: This is a "quasi-passive" verb. It describes a state of the subject ("Rice") rather than an action being performed by it. To convert this to a descriptive passive, we use the structure: [Subject] + [is/are] + [Adjective] + when + [it is] + [Past Participle].

questions.question: Roses smell sweet.[]
options: Roses are sweet smelling which someone smells.
Roses are sweet when smelt.
Roses are sweet when we smell.
Roses are smelling sweet.
questions.explanation: "smell" here is a linking verb describing the property of the subject. The passive construction isolates the quality ("are sweet") and defines the condition under which it is perceived ("when smelt").

questions.question: The house is building.[]
options: A house is being built by us.
The masons are building the house.
It is the house which is being built.
A house is being built.
questions.explanation: This is another "quasi-passive" structure. "The house is building" implies the house is undergoing the process of construction. In the standard passive voice, this requires the continuous form: [Object] + [is/are] + being + [Past Participle].

questions.question: It is time to shut up the shop.[]
options: It is time for the shop to be shut up.
It is time to be shut up the shop.
It is time to shut the shop up.
It is time the shop be shut up.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with "It is time to...," the passive conversion follows this specific structure: It is time + for + object + to be + past participle. The infinitive "to shut" becomes "to be shut."

questions.question: There are lots of things to do.[]
options: There are lots of things to done.
There are lots of things to be doing.
There are lots of things to be done.
None of them.
questions.explanation: In the active voice, the infinitive "to do" describes an action to be performed by someone. In the passive voice, it converts to "to be + past participle" (to be done) to indicate that the things must undergo the action.

questions.question: It is known to me how it was done by him.[]
options: I know how he has done.
I knew how he has done.
I knew how he did it.
I know how he did it.
questions.explanation:
This is a complex passive construction.
â"It is known to me" converts to the active "I know."
â"How it was done by him" converts to the active "how he did it."
âTogether, the active sentence is: "I know how he did it."

questions.question: Do it as I say.[]
options: Let it be done as is said by me.
Let it be done as I say.
It should be done as I say.
But it done as it is said.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence (a command). The standard passive structure for imperatives is: Let + object + be + past participle. The phrase "as I say" remains as a modifier at the end.

questions.question: Lord knew what they cost.[]
options: What they cost is known to Lord.
What they were cost is known to Lord.
What they are cost was known to Lord.
What they cost was known to Lord.
questions.explanation: This sentence consists of a main clause ("Lord knew") and a noun clause ("what they cost"). To make it passive, the entire noun clause becomes the subject, followed by the passive verb ("was known") and the agent ("to Lord").

questions.question: I know that he did the work.[]
options: It was known to me that the work was done by him.
It is known to me that the work was done by him.
It is known to me that the work has been done by him.
It was known to me that the work had been done by him.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with a subject followed by a clause (like "I know that..."), it is often converted into an impersonal passive structure: It + is/was + past participle + to + agent + [original clause converted to passive].

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: Two criminals were punished and one released.
Two criminals were punished and one was released.
Two criminals were punished when one released.
Two criminals were punished while one was released.
questions.explanation: When joining two passive clauses with a conjunction like "and," the verb (or auxiliary verb) must be repeated or clearly implied for both parts to maintain parallel grammatical structure. Since both actions happened in the past, "was" is needed to show that "released" is also in the passive voice.

questions.question: People know that the earth is round.[]
options: It is known that the earth is round.
It was known that the earth is round.
It was known that the earth was round.
It is knew that the earth was round.
questions.explanation: This follows the impersonal passive rule for general facts. When the active subject is generic ("People"), it is omitted in the passive voice. We use: It + [tense of the verb] + [past participle] + that-clause. Since "know" is present tense, we use "is known."

questions.question: I cannot depend on what you say.[]
options: What you say cannot be depended by me.
What is said by you cannot be depended on by me.
I cannot depend on what is said by you.
What is said cannot depended on by me.
questions.explanation: This sentence contains a prepositional phrase ("depend on"). In the passive voice, the preposition must remain attached to the verb ("depended on").

questions.question: One should keep one's promise.[]
options: One's promise should be kept.
A promise should be kept.
One's promise should be kept by one.
Promise should be kept.
questions.explanation: When the subject is an indefinite pronoun like "one," "someone," or "people," it is typically omitted in the passive voice. The structure follows: Object (A promise) + Modal (should) + be + past participle (kept).

questions.question: One should take care of one's health.[]
options: One's health should be taken care of.
One's health should be taken care of by one.
Health should be taken care of.
Health should be taken care.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, when the subject is a general pronoun like "one," it is usually omitted to keep the sentence concise. The structure is: Object (Health) + Modal (should) + be + Past Participle (taken) + preposition (care of).

questions.question: Somebody should have called the president this morning.[]
options: The president should have been called this morning.
The president could have been called this morning.
The president might have been called this morning.
The president could be called this morning.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the "should have + past participle" structure (modal perfect). To convert this to passive voice, we insert "been" after "have": Object (The president) + Modal Perfect (should have been) + Past Participle (called) + time (this morning).

questions.question: That house has not been lived in for years.[]
options: No one has been living in that house for years.
No one ever lived in that house for years.
Nobody has for years lived in that house.
Nobody had been living for years lived in that house.
questions.explanation: This is a conversion from passive to active. The passive agent ("Nobody" or "No one") becomes the subject. The passive verb "has not been lived in" reverts to the active present perfect "has lived."

questions.question: Nobody knows him here.[]
options: He is known by nobody here.
Nobody known him here.
He is not known here.
He is not known to nobody here.
questions.explanation: When the subject is a negative pronoun like "Nobody," the passive voice must negate the main verb. We use the structure: Object (He) + is/are + not + past participle (known) + place (here). We do not use "He is known by nobody," as that creates a double negative.

questions.question: He is not known here.[]
options: He is known here.
Nobody knows him here.
Everybody knows him here.
Somebody knows him here.
questions.explanation: This is the reverse of Q49. We take the passive statement and change it back to the active form. The "not known" becomes the active "knows," and the passive subject "He" becomes the object "him," with "Nobody" as the active subject.

questions.question: People always remember the patriots.[]
options: The patriot will always remembered by people.
The patriots are always being remembered.
People are always remembered by the patriots.
The patriots are always remembered.
questions.explanation: In the passive voice, the object ("patriots") becomes the subject. Because "remember" is in the simple present tense, we use the auxiliary "are" + past participle ("remembered").

questions.question: The people in Asia mainly eat rice.[]
options: Rice is mainly eaten in Asia.
Rice is mainly eaten by Asia.
Rice is mainly eaten for Asia.
Asia is mainly eaten by rice.
questions.explanation: The object "rice" becomes the subject. "Eat" is simple present, so it becomes "is eaten." The location ("in Asia") is kept to preserve meaning.

questions.question: The hut was burnt to ashes.[]
options: Ashes were burnt by the hut.
Fire burned the hut to ashes.
Fire burnt the hut to ashes.
Fire turned the hut to ashes.
questions.explanation: The passive sentence lacks an explicit agent. In English, the implied agent for "burnt" is usually "fire." To make it active, we place the agent (Fire) as the subject, followed by the active verb (burnt) and the object (the hut to ashes).

questions.question: Rome was not built in a day.(Active)[]
options: The Romans did not build Rome in a day.
People were not build Rome in a day.
The Romans were not build Rome in a day.
A day was not built by Rome.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Passive Voice (Past Indefinite). To change it to Active, we need a logical subject. Since "The Romans" built Rome, they become the subject. The structure follows: Subject + did not + verb (base form) + object.

questions.question: I shall be obliged to go.[]
options: Circumstances will oblige me to go.
I will be my obligation to go.
It will oblige me to go.
Obligation will make me go.
questions.explanation: This is a Passive Voice sentence where the agent (the cause) is omitted. In English grammar, "Circumstances" is the standard implied subject for the verb "oblige." When converting to Active, "Circumstances" takes the subject position, and the future tense "shall be obliged" becomes "will oblige."

questions.question: He wants me to do the work.[]
options: The work is wanted by him to go.
I am wanted to do the work by him.
He wants the work to be done by me.
I am to do the work is waned by him.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Active Voice containing an Infinitive (to do). When changing such sentences to Passive, the main verb (wants) remains unchanged, and the passive form is applied to the infinitive phrase. The structure follows: Subject + main verb + object + to be + Past Participle + by + agent.

questions.question: It was decided by him to sell the house.[]
options: He decided to sell the house.
He has decided to sell the house.
It was decided to sell the house.
He decided it to sell the house.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Passive Voice (Past Indefinite). To change it to Active, we move the agent (by him) to the subject position (He) and convert the verb to its simple past form. The structure follows: Subject + Verb (past form) + infinitive phrase.

questions.question: He decided to sell the house.[]
options: It was decided by him to sell the house.
He decided that the house shall be sold.
He decided that the house is sold.
He decided that the house is selling.
questions.explanation:
When an active sentence starts with "Subject + decided + to-infinitive,"the passive is often formed using the dummy subject "It."
The structure becomes:It + was/is + decided + by [agent] + to-infinitive.This maintains the focus on the decision itself.

questions.question: He decided to leave the job.[]
options: The job was decided to be left him.
He decided the job to be left.
He decided the job should be left.
The job should be left was decided by him.
questions.explanation: When an active sentence contains a verb of "deciding" followed by an infinitive with an object (to leave the job), the passive is formed by placing that object in a clause using "should be + past participle.

questions.question: He decided to sell the house.(Passive)[]
options: He told that the house is sold.
He wanted that the house should be sold.
He decided that the house may be sold by him.
He decided that the house should be sold.
questions.explanation: This uses a "that" clause to convert the infinitive phrase into the passive voice.The structure is: Subject + decided + that + object + should be + past participle.

questions.question: He suggested that smoking should be given up.[]
options: He suggested giving up smoking.
He has suggested giving up smoking.
He had suggested giving up smoking.
None of these.
questions.explanation: This is a passive-to-active conversion. When a passive sentence uses the structure "suggested that...should be + past participle," the active form uses the gerund (-ing) after the verb "suggest."

questions.question: Father advised giving up bad habits.[]
options: Bad habits are advised to give up by father.
Father advised that bad habits should be given up.
Bad habits should be given up by father.
Bad habits are advised to be given up by father.
questions.explanation: For verbs of "advising" or "suggesting" followed by a gerund (giving up), the passive is formed using a "that" clause + should be + past participle.

questions.question: He recommended using bulletproof jacket.[]
options: He recommended that bulletproof jacket should be used.
Bulletproof jacket should be used recommended.
He recommended for the use of bulletproof jacket.
Use of bulletproof jacket was recommended by him.
questions.explanation: Similar to "suggest" and "advise," when the verb "recommend" is followed by a gerund (using),the passive is formed by using a "that" clause + should be + past participle.

questions.question: I remember my sister taking me to the museum.[]
options: I remember I was taken to the museum by my sister.
I remember being taken to the museum by my sister.
I remember taken to the museum by my sister.
I remember myself being taken to the museum.
questions.explanation: When converting a sentence where the speaker is the object of a gerund phrase (taking me), the active gerund changes to a passive gerund (being + past participle).

questions.question: I don't like people telling me what to do.[]
options: I don't like being told what to do.
I don't like people being told what to do.
I don't like people are told what to do.
People are not liked by me to telling me what to do.
questions.explanation: When the speaker is the object of a gerund phrase (telling me), the passive is formed using a passive gerund (being + past participle). The general agent ("people") is removed, and "telling me" becomes "being told," keeping the focus on the speaker's feelings about the action.

questions.question: He is said to be very rich.[]
options: He said he is very rich.
People say he is very rich.
He said it is very rich.
People say it is very rich.
questions.explanation: This is a passive-to-active conversion of a reporting verb. The passive structure "Subject + is said + to be" is a formal way of expressing a general opinion. To make it active, we introduce a general subject like "People" or "They" followed by the active verb "say" and a "that" clause.

questions.question: They said he is a good candidate.[]
options: He was said to be a good candidate.
He was considered to be a good candidate.
It was said by them that he is to be a good candidate.
He was believed by them as a good candidate.
questions.explanation: When converting an active sentence with a reporting verb (said) and a "that" clause, the object of the clause (he) becomes the subject of the passive sentence. The structure follows: Subject + was/is + said + to be + complement.

questions.question: He died of fever.[]
options: Fever caused his to die.
Fever caused him to death.
He was caused to die of fever.
His death was caused with fever.
questions.explanation: This is a rare, formal conversion of an intransitive verb (died) into a passive-style causative structure. Since "died" cannot be directly passivized, we use the helping verb "caused" to create a passive voice effect: Subject + was + caused + to die + [reason].

questions.question: He worked for an hour.[]
options: An hour was worked for by him.
He was in the work for an hour.
An hour was passed by him in the work.
An hour was spent by him in working.
questions.explanation: The verb "worked" here is intransitive (it has no direct object). To create a passive effect, the sentence is restructured using the verb "spent." The time duration ("An hour") becomes the subject, resulting in: Time + was spent + by [agent] + in [gerund].

questions.question: I have a cat.[]
options: A cat is being had by me.
A cat is has been had by me.
A cat have been had by me.
A cat is had by me.
questions.explanation: The object ("a cat") becomes the subject, and the verb changes to is/am/are + past participle (had).

questions.question: I have a red cat.[]
options: A red cat is possessed by me.
A red cat is has been had by me.
A red cat belongs to me by me.
A red cat is to be had by me.
questions.explanation: While "have" often changes to "had" in passive voice (as seen in Q20), it is also common to replace it with the synonym "possessed" to avoid the awkwardness of the word "had." The structure remains Simple Present passive: Subject + is + possessed + by + agent

questions.question: I am sorry to disturb you.[]
options: I am sorry to be disturbed by you.
You are sorry to be disturbed by me.
I am sorry to have disturbed you.
I am disturbed by your sorrow.
questions.explanation: This conversion focuses on the aspect of the infinitive. To make the action of "disturbing" passive or completed in relation to the apology, the simple infinitive (to disturb) is changed to the perfect infinitive (to have disturbed).

questions.question: Let us go,you and I[]
options: Let you and I be gone.
Let's you and I are gone.
You and I should go now.
Let's go then,should we ?
questions.explanation: For imperative sentences starting with "Let," the passive is formed using the structure: Let + Object + be + Past Participle.

questions.question: When should we use passive sentence ?[]
options: When the doer is less important.
When the doer is more important.
When the subject is very short.
When we use in informal style.
questions.explanation: The primary purpose of the passive voice is to shift focus. We use it when the action or the receiver of the action is the main point, or when the doer (agent) is unknown, obvious, or simply less important than the result.

questions.question: That house was built ten years ago.(Active)[]
options: Someone built the house ten years ago.
We had built the house ten years ago.
Somebody had built the house ten years ago.
They built the house ten years ago.
questions.explanation: This is a passive-to-active conversion where the original agent is missing. When the doer is unknown or vague, we use an indefinite pronoun like "Someone" as the subject. The passive "was built" (Simple Past) reverts to the active form "built."

questions.question: I saw him fall from the tree.[]
options: He was seen by me to fall from the tree.
The tree was seen to fall by me.
He was seen to fall from the tree.
He was seen falling from the tree by me.
questions.explanation: When a verb of perception (see, hear, watch) is followed by a bare infinitive (fall) in the active voice, it changes to a "to-infinitive" (to fall) in the passive voice. The object "him" becomes the subject "He," resulting in: Subject + was seen + to + verb.

questions.question: I saw him play.(Passive)[]
options: He was seen by me play.
Play was seen him by me.
He was seen playing by me.
He was seen to play by me.
questions.explanation: When a verb of perception like "saw" is followed by a bare infinitive (play) in the active voice, you must use a to-infinitive (to play) in the passive voice.

questions.question: I saw him go to the garden.(Passive)[]
options: He was seen go to the garden.
He was seen to go to the garden.
He went to the garden was seen.
He was been seen to go to the garden.
questions.explanation: the active bare infinitive (go) must be converted to a to-infinitive (to go) when changing to the passive voice. The structure is: Subject (He) + was seen + to-infinitive (to go) + rest of the sentence.

questions.question: Why is a noble made ?[]
options: Why do they make a noise ?
Why has a noise made ?
Why is made a noise them ?
Why they are making noise ?
questions.explanation: This is a passive-to-active conversion of an interrogative sentence. The passive "is... made" indicates a Simple Present tense. To make it active, we add a general subject (they) and use the helping verb "do" for the question format.

questions.question: Who spoke it ?(passive)[]
options: It was spoken by whom ?
By whom was it spoken ?
By whom it has spoken ?
By whom it was spoken ?
questions.explanation: For questions starting with "Who," the passive voice typically begins with "By whom." Since "spoke" is Simple Past, the structure becomes: By whom + was/were + object + past participle (spoken).

questions.question: The unfed should be fed.[]
options: Feed the unfed.
We should feed the unfed.
Please feed the unfed.
They should be feeding the unfed.
questions.explanation: When a passive sentence uses "should be + past participle" to give a command or strong suggestion, the active version is often a direct Imperative sentence."Should be fed" simply becomes the base verb "Feed."

questions.question: One should read only what one likes.[]
options: What one likes should be read only.
What one likes should read only.
What one likes should have read only.
None of the above.
questions.explanation: In this sentence, the entire clause "what one likes" acts as the object. To make it passive, this clause becomes the subject, followed by the passive modal structure: should + be + past participle (read).

questions.question: His comment surprised me.[]
options: I was surprised by his comment.
I was surprised at his comment.
I was surprised for his comment.
I was surprised to his comment.
questions.explanation: For the verb "surprise," the standard preposition is "at" when reacting to an event or statement. The structure is: Subject + was + surprised + at + [trigger].

questions.question: Salina was stitching a pant.[]
options: A pant was being stitch by Salina.
A pant has been made by Salina.
A pant was stitched by Salina.
A pant was being stitched by Salina.
questions.explanation: The active sentence is in the Past Continuous tense (was stitching). To make it passive, we use the formula: was/were + being + past participle.

questions.question: Nobody believes a liar.[]
options: A liar is never believed by anyone.
A liar should not be believed by anybody.
A liar is not believed by anybody.
A liar is believed by nobody.
questions.explanation: When an active sentence uses a negative subject like "Nobody," the passive version usually changes the subject to an affirmative one (anybody) and makes the verb negative (is not).

questions.question: His sudden death shocked me.[]
options: I was shocked by his sudden death.
I was shocked to his sudden death.
I was shocked to know his sudden death.
I was shocked at his sudden death.
questions.explanation: When changing to Passive Voice, verbs expressing a reaction to an event (like shocked, surprised, astonished, alarmed) typically take the preposition "at" instead of "by."

questions.question: I was surprised to see that he had been beaten black and blue.[]
options: I was surprised to see that he has been beaten black and blue.
It surprised me to see that he had been beaten black and blue.
It was surprising that he had been beaten black and blue.
Then he had been beaten black and blue was surprising.
questions.explanation: The original sentence is in the Passive Voice. To convert it to Active Voice, the infinitive phrase "to see that..." acts as the functional subject. In standard English, this is often phrased using the dummy subject "It" to lead the active verb (surprised) followed by the object (me).

questions.question: Do you see the flower ?[]

Is the flower being seen by you ?
Has the flower was seen by you ?
Is the flower seen by you ?
questions.explanation:
When the sentence converting to passive,the auxiliary "Do" is replaced by Is/Am/Are based on the new subject (the flower), followed by the past participle (seen).
Is + Subject (the flower) + V3 (seen) + by + Object (you)?

questions.question: They elected him captain.[]

He was elected captain by them.
Captain is elected him by them.
He has been elected captain by them.

Structure:Subject (He) + was + V3 (elected) + complement (captain) + by + Object (them).

questions.question: I have killed the bird.[]

[Object] + has/have + been + Past Participle (V3) + by [Subject]

questions.question: Please close the door.[]

You are requested to close the door.
The door is to be closed.
I request you to close the door.
questions.explanation: When an imperative sentence starts with or implies "Please," the passive form typically uses the introductory phrase "You are requested to..." followed by the base verb.

questions.question: Please keep quiet.[]

You are requested for keep quiet.
You are asked to keep quiet.
You are told to keep quiet.

questions.question: Don't waste your time.[]

questions.question: The trainer walked the horse after the race.[]

questions.question: Let me do the sum.[]

Let the sum done by me.
Let the sum being done by me.
Let the sum be done by me.

questions.question: It is impossible to do this.[]
options: Doing this is impossible.
This is impossible to be done.
This is must be done.
This cannot be done.

questions.question: It cannot be done.(Active)[]

questions.question: What cannot be cured must be endured.(Active)[]

We cannot cure what must endure.

We must endure what we cannot cure.

questions.question: The cat is running after the rat.(Passive)[]

The cat is being run after by the rat.
The cat is run after by the rat.
The cat is being run after by the rat.

questions.question: Mend your ways.(passive)[]

Your ways should be mended.

Let your ways are mended.

questions.question: Who killed the bird ?[]

Who was killed by the bird ?

questions.question: He is called a genius.[]

questions.question: The critic wrote a scathing review.[]

A scathing review written by the critic.

questions.question: We ought to have saved our environment.[]

questions.question: She does not like eating too much.[]

questions.question: English is spoken all over the world.[]

questions.question: Your blame counts for nothing.[]

A bird was being stalked by a cat in my garden.

questions.question: Why wasn't the matter brought to my notice ?[]

questions.question: Didn't she know anything about the Sundarbans ?[]
options: Was nothing about Sundarbans known to her ?

Was she not known nothing about the Sundarbans ?

questions.explanation: In Passive, "anything" changes to "nothing" to maintain the negative sense, or remains "anything" with a negative verb. "Known" is followed by the preposition "to"

questions.question: She plucked some flowers.[]
options: Some flowers are plucked by her.
Some flowers were plucked by her.
She was plucked some flowers.
Some flowers had been plucked by her.
questions.explanation: Simple Past tense. The object "some flowers" (plural) takes "were" + V3 (plucked).

questions.question: I was deceived by the stranger.[]
options: The stranger deceives me.
The stranger has deceived me.
The stranger had deceived me.
The stranger deceived me.
questions.explanation: Passive to Active (Simple Past). The agent "the stranger" becomes the subject, followed by the V2 form of the verb "deceived" and the object "me."

questions.question: We do not hate the poor.[]
options: The poor are not hated by us.
The poor is not hated by us.
We are not hated by the poor.
The poor is not done to be hated by us.
questions.explanation: Simple Present negative. "The poor" is treated as a plural noun, so it takes "are not" + V3 (hated).

questions.question: Fire burnt the ship.[]
options: The ship was burnt by fire.
The ship was burnt.
The ship was burnt with fire.
The ship was burnt to fire.
questions.explanation: Simple Past. The object "the ship" becomes the subject + "was" + V3 (burnt). In many contexts, the agent "by fire" can be omitted if the result is the focus.

questions.question: Who was helped by you ? (Active)[]
options: Who was helped by you ?
Who did help you ?
Whom did you help ?
Who helped you ?
questions.explanation: Passive to Active. "By you" becomes the subject "you." Since it is Simple Past, the question uses the auxiliary "did" + V1

questions.question: Don't laugh at me.[]
options: Let me be laughed at.
Let me be not laughed at.
I am laughed at.
Let me be not laughed.
questions.explanation: Imperative negative. The structure is: Let + object (me) + be + not + V3 (laughed at).

questions.question: Who gave this book to you ?[]
options: Whom was the book given to you ?
By whom was the book given to you ?
To whom was the book given to you ?
None
questions.explanation: Interrogative starting with "Who." "Who" changes to "By whom." Since "gave" is Simple Past, the structure is: By whom + was + object (the book) + V3 (given).

questions.question: Who gave you the pen ?[]
options: By whom you were given the pen ?
Who were given you the pen ?
By whom were you given the pen ?
By whom the pen was given to you ?
questions.explanation: Here using the indirect object "you" as the subject. By whom + were (matching "you") + you + V3 (given) + the pen?

questions.question: Whom did you know there ?[]
options: Who was known to you there ?
By whom you knew there ?
To whom you know there ?
Who was known by you there ?
questions.explanation: "Whom" (object) becomes "Who" (subject) in Passive. The verb "know" in Simple Past becomes "was known." Note: "Known" takes the preposition "to," not "by."

questions.question: I am to make a telephone call.[]
options: A telephone call is to be made by me.
A telephone call is to making by me.
A telephone call will to make by me.
A telephone call will made by me.
questions.explanation: Sentences with "am/is/are + to + verb" use the passive form: Object + am/is/are + to be + V3.

questions.question: I know what he thinks.[]
options: What he think was know to me.
What he thinks was know to me.
What he thinks is known to me.
He think was is know to me.
questions.explanation: The object is the entire clause "what he thinks." This clause acts as a singular subject: [What he thinks] + is (Present) + known + to me.

questions.question: I was compelled to do it.[]
options: Circumstances compelled me to do it.
compelled to do.
Compelling easy but difficult to do.
He was compelled.
questions.explanation: Passive to Active. The agent is missing but implied (usually "circumstances"). To make it active, use: Subject (Circumstances) + V2 (compelled) + object (me) + to do it.

questions.question: The news shocked him[]
options: He was shocked by the news.
He was shocked at the news.
He was shocked with the news.
He was shocked on the news.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Past, the object "him" becomes the subject "he". Certain verbs like "shocked," "surprised," or "alarmed" take the preposition "at" instead of "by" when referring to a thing or news.

questions.question: He does not like people laughing at him.[]
options: People laughing at him are not liked by him.
He does not like being laughed at.
To be laughed at by people are not like by him.
He does not like him being laughed at by people.
questions.explanation: When "like/dislike" is followed by a gerund phrase, we change the gerund to its passive form: being + V3. The subject "He" and the main verb "does not like" remain.

questions.question: Please grant me two days' leave.(Passive)[]
options: Let me be granted two days' leave.
Let me two days leave be granted.
May I please be granted two days' leave ?
I may be granted two days' leave.
questions.explanation: For polite imperative requests starting with "Please," the passive can be formed using a request structure: "May I + [please/kindly] + be + V3."

questions.question: Nobody trusts a traitor. (Passive)[]
options: A traitor is trusted.
A traitor should not be trusted.
Everybody hates a traitor.
A traitor is not trusted by anybody.
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present negative sentence. To maintain the "Nobody" (negative) sense in passive voice, "Nobody" is replaced by "not... by anybody." The structure is: Object (A traitor) + is + not + V3 (trusted) + by anybody.

questions.question: Change the voice : Kindly grant me two days' leave.[]
options: May I kindly be granted two days' leave ?
Let me be granted two days' leave.
Let two days' leave be granted to me.
Two days' leave is requested to me.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence expressing a request (indicated by "Kindly"). In passive voice, formal requests are often transformed using the modal "May" to maintain politeness. The structure becomes: May + Subject (I) + kindly + be + V3 (granted) + Object (two days' leave).

questions.question: I helped her solve the problem.(Passive)[]
options: She was helped to solve the problem.
The problem was solved by me.
Her problem was solved by me.
She was helped to solve the problem by me.
questions.explanation:
The sentence is in the Simple Past tense (helped). When converting to passive, the object (her) becomes the subject (She).The bare infinitive (solve) in the active voice must change to a full infinitive (to solve) in the passive voice.
âStructure: Subject + was/were + helped + to + Verb + by + Agent.

questions.question: He saw me do it.[]
options: I was seen do it by him.
I was seen to do it by him.
I was seen doing it by him.
I was seen to doing it by him.
questions.explanation:
This sentence uses a verb of perception (saw).In the active voice,these are followed by a bare infinitive(do).However,in the passive voice, they require a "to" infinitive (to do).The object (me) becomes the subject (I),and the past tense verb (saw) becomes was seen.
âStructure: Subject + was/were + seen + to + Verb + by + Agent.

questions.question: Never tell a lie.[]
options: Let never a lie be told.
Let not a lie never be told.
Let a lie never be told.
Let lie never be told.
questions.explanation: This is a negative imperative sentence. When using "Never", the passive structure follows the pattern: Let + never + object + be + V3

questions.question: Never a tell a lie.[]
options: Let not a lie ever be told.
Let a lie never be told.
Let a lie not ever be told.
Let never be told a lie.
questions.explanation: This is a negative imperative sentence. When using "Never", the passive structure follows the pattern: Let + never + object + be + V3

questions.question: Do you know him ? (Passive)[]
options: Is he known by you ?
Is he known to you ?
Does he known by you ?
Is he known with you ?
questions.explanation:
The "Know" Rule: Unlike most verbs that use "by" (e.g., done by, seen by), the verb know must be followed by "to".
âStructure: Is/Am/Are + Subject + known + to + Agent?

questions.question: Do you find your payment too little ? (Passive)[]
options: Is your payment found too little to you ?

Are your payment found too little by you ?
Is your payment found too little by you ?
questions.explanation:
This is an Interrogative sentence in the Simple Present tense.Unlike the verb "know" (which uses to),the verb "find" follows the standard rule of using "by" for the agent.
âStructure: Is/Am/Are + Object + Past Participle (V3) + Adjective + by + Subject

questions.question: Some Children are helping the wounded man.[]
options: The wounded man was helped by some Children.
The wounded man was helping by some Children.
The wounded man was to be helped by some Children.
The wounded man is being helped by some Children.
questions.explanation:
âThis sentence is in the Present Continuous tense (are helping). To keep the "continuous" meaning in the passive voice, we must use the word "being".
âStructure: Object + is/am/are + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject

questions.question: He is going to give me a prize.[]
options: I am going to give a prize by him.
I am gone to give a prize by him.
I was going to be given a prize by him.
I am going to be given a prize by him.
questions.explanation: This sentence uses the "going to" future construction followed by an infinitive (give). In passive voice, the "going to" part remains the same, but the infinitive changes to be + V3.

questions.question: The gate was opened by the poem.[]
options: The poem opened the gate.
The poem had opened the gate.
The poem has opened the gate.
The poem opens the gate.
questions.explanation:
This is a Passive to Active conversion.The sentence is in the Simple Past passive form (was opened).
âStructure (Passive): Object + was/were + V3 + by + Agent
âStructure (Active): Agent + Past Tense Verb (V2) + Object

questions.question: They laugh at us.[]

We are laughed by them.
We are laughed at by them.
questions.explanation:

âStructure: Object + am/is/are + Past Participle (V3) + Preposition + by + Subject

questions.question: Shelia was writing a letter.[]

A letter was been written by Shelia.
questions.explanation:
To keep the "continuous" aspect in passive voice, you must use the word "being".
âStructure: Object + was/were + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject

questions.question: He taught me to read Arabic.[]

I had been taught by him to read Arabic.
I was being taught to read Arabic.
questions.explanation:
This sentence is in the Simple Past tense (taught). It contains a direct object (Arabic) and an indirect object (me).
âStructure: Subject (Person) + was/were + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent + Infinitive phrase

questions.question: He made me drive the car.[]

I am made to drive his car by him.

âStructure: Subject + was/were + made + to + Verb + Object + by + Agent

questions.question: Who has broken the glass ? (Passive)[]

By whom has the glass been broken ?
questions.explanation:
Questions starting with "Who" change to "By whom" in the passive voice.

questions.question: Do not laugh at the poor (passive)[]

Let the poor be laugh at.

questions.question: We made her recite a poem.[]

A poem was made to be recited.

In active voice, the verb "make" is followed by a bare infinitive (recite). In passive voice, it must change to a full infinitive (to recite).
âStructure: Subject + was/were + made + to + Verb + Object + by + Agent

questions.question: Did the boy catch the bird ?[]
options: Was the bird caught by the boy ?
Was the bird being caught by the boy ?
Is the bird caught by the boy ?
Has the bird been caught by the boy ?
questions.explanation: This is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past tense. To convert it to passive voice, we use the structure: Was/Were + subject (the bird) + past participle (caught) + by + agent (the boy)?

questions.question: BBC broadcast the news.[]
options: The news are broadcasted by BBC.

The news is broadcast by BBC.
The news was broadcast by BBC.

questions.question: Who broke the pencil ?[]
options: By whom the pencil was broken ?
By whom was the pencil broken ?
The pencil was broken by whom ?
Who was broken the pencil ?
questions.explanation: When an active sentence starts with "Who", it usually changes to "By whom" in the passive voice. Since the sentence is in the Simple Past, we use the structure: By whom + was/were + object (the pencil) + past participle (broken)?

questions.question: Let the book be read by you.[]
options: Read the book.
You are to read the book.
Let the book read by you.
Let the book be reading by you.
questions.explanation: This is a conversion from passive to active voice for an imperative sentence (a command). The passive structure "Let + object + be + V3" is the standard way to represent a direct command like "Read the book" in passive form.

questions.question: Who will help you ?[]
options: By whom will you be helped ?
By whom you will be helped ?
By whom would you be helped ?
By whom will be you helped ?
questions.explanation:
For interrogative sentences starting with "Who" in the Simple Future tense, the passive structure is: By whom + will + object (you) + be + V3 (helped)?

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: The matter was informed in the police.
The matter had been informed of the police.
The police were informed of the matter.
The police was informed of the matter.

questions.question: He did not tell the dangerous secret to anybody.[]

The dangerous secret was told not him to anybody.
Anybody was not told about the dangerous secret by him.

questions.question: We insist on punctuality in this office.[]
options: Punctuality is insisted on in this office.
Punctuality be insisted in this office.
Punctuality should be insisted in this office.
Punctuality is to be insisted on in this office.
questions.explanation: This is in the Simple Present tense. When a verb is followed by a fixed preposition (like insist on), that preposition must stay with the verb in the passive voice. The structure is: Subject (Punctuality) + is + V3 (insisted) + on + remaining part of the sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: By whom it is painted ?
By whom it is painted with ?
Who was it painted by ?
With whom it is painted by ?
questions.explanation: This is a passive question. While "By whom" is formally correct, the structure in option A is missing the question word order (it should be "By whom is it painted?"). Option C uses the common modern structure: Who + auxiliary verb + subject + V3 + preposition (by)?

questions.question: Don't take the forget me not.[]

Let not the forget me not be taken by you.
Let never taken the forget me not.
Let not taken by you the forget me not.

questions.question: Who is calling me ?[]

By whom I am being called ?
By whom am I being called ?
By whom have I being called ?

questions.question: Buy me a shirt.[]
options: Let a shirt be bought.
Let a shirt be bought for me.
Let bought a shirt for me.
Let buy a shirt for me.
questions.explanation: This is an imperative sentence with a direct object (a shirt) and an indirect object (me). The standard passive form is: Let + direct object (a shirt) + be + V3 (bought) + for + indirect object (me).

questions.question: I know him.[]
options: He was known to me.
He is known to me.
I was known to him.
He known to me.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Present, "know" changes to "is known." Crucially, the verb "know" takes the preposition "to" in the passive voice instead of the usual "by.

questions.question: Who did it ?[]
options: By whom had it been done ?
By whom was it done ?
Who is it done by ?
By whom has it been done ?
questions.explanation: This is in the Simple Past. The structure is: By whom + was/were + object (it) + V3 (done)?

questions.question: He has a cow.[]
options: A cow is had by him.
A cow is have by him.
A cow have been by him.
A cow has been by him.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Present, the verb "has" (possession) is converted to the passive form "is had." The object "a cow" becomes the subject, followed by the auxiliary verb "is" and the past participle "had."

questions.question: What is wanted by him ?[]
options: What do he want ?
What did he want ?
What does he want ?
What is he wants ?
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present passive question. To convert it to active, use the interrogative structure: What + do/does + subject (he) + base verb (want)?

questions.question: I was brightly addressed by her.[]
options: She addressed me brightly.
She has addressed me brightly.
She addresses me brightly.
I was addressed by her brightly.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the Simple Past passive ("was addressed"). To change it to active, the agent "her" becomes the subject "She," followed by the past tense verb "addressed" and the object "me."

questions.question: Let us write a letter.[]
options: Let a letter to write by us.
Let a letter be wrote by us.
Let a letter be written by us.
Let a letter written by us.
questions.explanation: For "Let us..." imperative sentences, the passive structure is: Let + object (a letter) + be + V3 (written) + by + us.

questions.question: You will be helped by me ?[]
options: I shall help you.
I must help you.
I shall have helped you.
I should help you.
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Future passive sentence. In the active voice, the subject "I" typically pairs with the auxiliary "shall" (or "will"), followed by the base verb "help" and the object "you."

questions.question: Am I wanted by you ?[]
options: Did you want me ?
Do you want me ?
Are you wanted me ?
Have you wanted me ?
questions.explanation: This is a Simple Present passive question. To make it active, use the structure: Do/Does + subject (you) + base verb (want) + object (me)?

questions.question: The teacher will be teaching us.[]

We will be taught by the teacher.
We shall be being taught by the teacher.
We will be being taught by the teacher.

questions.question: Karim told Rahim to give up smoking.[]

Karim was told to give up smoking.
Rahim is told to give up smoking.
Karim requested Rahim to give up smoking.

questions.question: He teaches us English.[]

English was teaching us by him.

questions.question: What did they pay you for doing the job ?[]

questions.question: He satisfied everybody. (Passive)[]

Everybody would be satisfied at him.

questions.question: The sudden noise frightened the horse.[]

The horse frightened the noise suddenly.
The horse was frightened by the sudden noise.

questions.question: Who will pay him ?[]

By whom you will be paid ?

questions.question: Who is creating the mess ?[]

questions.question: Health should be taken care of.[]

questions.question: He did not give up the fight even though he was badly bruised.[]

The fight was not given up by him even though he was badly bruised.

questions.question: Who killed the bird ? (Passive)[]

Who was the bird killed by ?
By whom was killed the bird ?
questions.explanation: This is a variation of the passive question format. Instead of starting with "By whom," it uses: Who + auxiliary (was) + object (the bird) + V3 (killed) + by?

questions.question: Shubho ate four pieces of Hilsha fish at dinner. (Passive)[]

questions.question: Whom were you calling ? (Passive)[]
